title: Tree Height
statement: Return the number of nodes on the longest path from the root to a leaf. An empty tree has depth 0.
constraints: Trees are encoded in level order with null gaps.

brute_force_solution:
def tree_max_depth(root):
    level = [] if root is None else [root]
    depth = 0
    while level:
        depth += 1
        level = [child for node in level for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]
    return depth
hints: Depth counts nodes, not edges; the empty subtree contributes zero.
The recursive rule is 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). For a deep chain, represent the pending work explicitly instead of nesting Python calls.
Put (root,1) on a stack. Pop a node and its depth, update the largest depth, and push existing children with depth+1.
An explicit depth-first stack preserves the recursive traversal while supporting the full 20,000-node limit without changing Python's recursion limit.
editorial: The recursive relationship is depth(node)=1+max(depth(left),depth(right)), with zero for an empty tree. Direct Python recursion can overflow on a valid long chain, so the reference records (node,depth) frames in an explicit stack and takes the largest depth visited. Every node is processed once, and at most O(h) pending frames are needed for height h. An independent breadth-first oracle counts successive levels instead. Version 2 keeps the original signature, node-count convention, ID, and saved progress while adding deep-chain and wide-tree checks.
